newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST - Gloomy future seen for Smurfit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Gloomy future seen for Smurfit.

text.p: Things are expected to get worse before they get better for Ireland's Jefferson Smurfit Group Plc, the packaging giant which is tipped to report a drop of up to 50 percent in first half pretax profits on Tuesday.
Analysts say an even gloomier year may be in prospect for the world's leading producer of corrugated packaging materials, hard hit by world pricing pressures on its sector.
"It may be 1998 before the company sees recovery feeding through to the bottom line," one analyst said.
He said pricing pressures within the paper and packaging industry were weighing heavily on the sector.
"Profits have dropped because prices have fallen, it is as simple as that. Smurfit is no exception, merely another casualty in a very cyclical sector," one equity dealer said.
Analysts' profit forecasts for first half 1996 range from 110 to 130 million punts for the 3.0 billion punt company compared to 201 million for the same period in 1995.
"At the pre-tax line we are forecasting about 110 million punts and earnings per share (EPS) of 7.1 pence," UBS securities analyst Ethan Dempsey told Reuters.
UBS expects full-year pre-tax profits of 200 million punts and 12.9 pence earnings per share (EPS).

Davy stockbrokers analyst Joe Burnell allows for a more favourable bias in the first half, forecasting 130 million punts at the pre-tax level and 8.0 pence ESP but is expecting the second half pre-tax number to drop to 80 million, giving a full year outturn of 210 million punts and 13 pence EPS.
Some analysts believe negative pricing within the sector may still not have bottomed out although others hold out a tentative hope that the worst is over.
Even if there is an upturn in pricing trends analysts said it will take time to feed into the price of corrugated boxes, Smurfit's core product.
Davy's Burnell is expecting Smurfit's pre-tax profits to bottom out in 1997. He is forecasting a pre-tax outturn of 130 million punts and EPS of 9.0 pence for the full year.
